results.note: Introduction restatement of Theorem A (metrization plus completeness). No standalone proof here.
Introduction restatement of Theorem B; third bullet is the plurifunctional extension later stated as prop_functionals.
Relative finite-energy class E^1_{X/Y}(L) defined by a fiberwise condition.
Extension of Deligne pairings to relative finite-energy metrics; change-of-metric formula retained, curvature formula explicitly not claimed (line 296).

Author: 'This is a very standard result, which follows from e.g. the arguments of [bjtrivval21, Th. 5.8], therefore we leave the details to the interested reader.' Citation pointer only, no author proof. Used inside the proof of r_thm_eonepairing.
Relative maximality: Sadullaev maximality on every pi^{-1}(U).
S^1-invariant relative maximality equals 'geodesic' in the sense of [bbj].
Existence and uniqueness of a continuous relatively maximal extension; existence of a subsolution under hyperconvexity. Proof has two internal \subsubsection* parts.
Relative maximality iff (dd^c phi)^{d+1}=0 iff equality with the Perron-Bremmermann envelope; proof cites [complexmaeq, Th. 2.20].
Relative maximality on U iff zero curvature of the restricted Deligne pairing <phi^{d+1}>_{X/Y}; uses thm_existencemaximal and decreasing-net continuity of the pairing.
Signed generalized Lelong number nu_0 with the +a log|z| normalization.
Concavity-type estimate f(z) <= nu_0(f) log|z| + sup_{|z|=1} f; complete elementary proof.
Four equivalent characterizations of logarithmic growth, including the O(log|z|) bound (iii)/(iv) used later.
Relative dimension zero: PSH = log-growth subharmonic, maximal = harmonic; notes that maximality plus finite energy no longer forces log growth.
Pushforward of relative maximality to the base via the Deligne pairing; proof invokes prop_harmonicitymaximaldiscs and the relative-dimension-zero examples.
Metrization of \hat E^1(L) by the generalized slope of z -> d_1(phi_{0,z},phi_{1,z}); its proof is placed at 742-770 after the subharmonicity proposition and the uniform-control lemma.

Key new mechanism: superharmonicity of the Deligne pairing of the rooftop envelope via relatively maximal extensions on discs and the reverse mean-value inequality, plus logarithmic growth from lem_extpshtame.
Fiberwise bound d_1 <= \hat d_1(-log|z|) and nonnegativity; links the base-locally uniform topology to \hat d_1. Used for completeness and for closedness.

Headline Theorem A, second half. Proof at 795-803 is a short combination of lem_unifcontrol, the cited fiberwise completeness [darbook, Th. 3.36] and prop_closed; no new construction or estimate beyond candidate jep229-lelong-metrization-hatE1.
Defines the C^0_{X,loc}-d_1 and C^0_{X/D*,loc}-d_1 topologies.
Closedness of \hat E^1(L) in the base-locally uniform d_1 topology; zero curvature is stable under uniform limits.

Maximal envelope \hat P for continuous finite-energy metrics with d_1 = o(log|z|), giving a projection C^0 cap E^1 -> C^0 cap \hat E^1. Uses annuli, monotone harmonic convergence and equality of slopes. Auxiliary to a pseudodistance construction, not part of Theorems A/B.
Pseudodistance via \hat P; stated as an immediate corollary, no proof.
Author notes the construction does not a priori extend to all of E^1(L) because of convergence problems for Lelong numbers under decreasing limits.
Non-Archimedean psh = decreasing limits of psh model metrics; a model metric is psh iff the model is relatively nef.
Attributed to [bfjsemi]: phi_L + log|a| is psh when L tensor a is globally generated. No author proof in this work.

Construction of (.)^NA: PSH(L) -> PSH(L_K^an) from generic Lelong numbers along vertical divisors; lower semicontinuous and order preserving. Proof is the prose block 966-996 (no proof environment), with multiplier-ideal preliminaries at 929-954.
Verticality of multiplier ideals plus a uniform m_0 making (m+m_0)L tensor J(m phi) globally generated; uses Skoda, relative Castelnuovo-Mumford, Nadel vanishing.
phi extends to a psh metric on a model iff phi^NA <= phi_M; equality when the extension is locally bounded. Used in thm_delignelelong and thm_uniquenesstropmaxdisc.

Monge-Ampère extension property for metrics with a locally bounded extension: equality of the NA limit of <phi^{d+1}> and <(phi^NA)^{d+1}>. Short proof via prop_extension_on_model and vanishing of nu_0(u).
Hybrid maximal: relative maximality plus maximality against psi with psi^NA <= phi^NA and the boundary limsup condition.
Existence and uniqueness of phi in \hat E^1(L) with prescribed phi^NA in E^1(L_K^an), plus the one-sided inequality for the Monge-Ampère energy. Proof has four named steps (1119, 1132, 1151, 1177).

The inverse of (.)^NA is an isometric embedding of (E^1(L^an), d_1^NA) onto \hat E^1_hyb(L); completeness and geodesicity follow; the core identity is the Lelong number of the rooftop Deligne pairing, constructed via annuli.

Plurifunctional extension for tuples of hybrid maximal metrics. Proof at 1283-1305 is explicitly a sketch; the quantitative inequality is imported from [bbj, App. A, Lem. A.2] and [liytd, S4] via the I-functional; no self-contained author derivation of the exponent 2^{-n} estimate.

Sequence of distance-preserving maps for test configurations; the proof assembles thm_isometry and [bbj, Th. 6.6] and explicitly leaves the distance-preserving verification to the interested reader (line 1342).
Conjecture psi^NA = P(phi)^NA = Phi^NA for Calabi-Yau degenerations; not a proved result.

proof_blocks.notes: Induction on the number n of non-continuous metrics; monotone convergence of pairings; the text says uniqueness follows from the change-of-metric formula, 'which itself shows that the construction glues well over X' although the base is Y.

Nested \subsubsection* at 362 (first point: continuity of the Perron-Bremmermann envelope via a Laplacian barrier and Dini) and at 395 (second point: Bergman kernel approximation with pi^*rho compensation).
Cites [complexmaeq, Th. 2.20].
Continuous case via (dd^c phi)^{d+1}=0; general case by decreasing regularization plus thm_existencemaximal.
Convexity of the sup on circles.
Dominating model and Cartier divisor D with pi_X^*L + D = pi_Y^*M.
Characterization (iv) plus Demailly regularization.
Two lines; invokes prop_harmonicitymaximaldiscs and examples exa_reldim, exa_reldim2.
Superharmonicity of <P(phi0,phi1)^{d+1}> via disc extensions psi and the mean-value inequality, then logarithmic growth via lem_extpshtame(iv) and the triangle inequality.

Separated from the statement (673-675) by prop_distancesubharmonic and lem_unifcontrol. Symmetry and definiteness from lem_unifcontrol; triangle inequality by comparing generalized slopes with additive constants a_ij.
A uniform limit of zero-curvature metrics has zero curvature; applies prop_harmonicitymaximaldiscs.
Cauchy -> fiberwise d_1 Cauchy by lem_unifcontrol -> fiberwise limit by [darbook, Th. 3.36] -> closedness by prop_closed.

Annuli U_r, increasing sequence phi_{r,z}, monotone harmonic convergence of u_r to u, slope equality nu_0(u)=nu_0(v). The author says the convex-to-subharmonic adaptation is left to the interested reader (line 828).
Skoda, relative Castelnuovo-Mumford, Kodaira/Nadel vanishing.
Decreasing approximation and nesting of multiplier ideals.
Common domination Z, Cartier divisor D, comparison of generic Lelong numbers; the converse uses uniqueness of the Siu decomposition.
Locally bounded extension implies phi^NA = phi_L and nu_0(u)=0.
Four steps with \subsubsection* headers at 1132 (Lelong inequality for MA energies), 1151 (general model net), 1177 (the E^1 case); the first step is the ample-model envelope.

Assumes the isometry; completeness and geodesicity from thm_1completeness and [reb20b, Th. A]; core: annuli metrics psi_r, the envelope identity P(phi0^NA,phi1^NA)=psi^NA, and harmonic averages linear in log r.
Explicitly a sketch ('which we sketch now'); the bound I_i <= C d_1^{2^{-n}} D(z) is cited from [bbj, Lem. A.2] and the I-term bound C' log|z| as in [liytd, S4].
First map by [bbj, Th. 6.6]; middle map injective; distance preservation is 'essentially a simpler version' of thm_isometry and is left to the interested reader (1342).

source_notation_points.phenomenon: The introduction writes d_{1,z}(phi0,phi1)=E(phi0)-E(phi1)+2E(P(phi0,phi1)) while line 255 writes d_1(phi0,phi1)=E(phi0)+E(phi1)-2E(P(phi0,phi1)); the E signs differ. Recorded as a literal source phenomenon; no correction made.

The theorem statement uses \hat d_1 = nu_0(d_1(...)) without a minus sign, whereas the defining display at 670 uses \hat d_1 := -\nu_0(d_1(...)); lem_unifcontrol and the abstract rely on the convention with the minus sign. Literal discrepancy recorded only.
The proof says the construction 'glues well over $X$' although the base of the pairing is Y.
The induction refers to 'indices i in {0,...,d+1}' and 'd+1>n>0', while only d+1 indices 0,...,d exist; later ranges use d+1-n and d+2-n. Literal range notation recorded; no repair.
Immediately after thm_eonepairing the author notes that the curvature formula (eq_ddc) will not hold in general for the extended pairing.
The symbol a denotes both the centre of the disc D(a,r) (line 690) and the real constant in the logarithmic-growth bound (lines 715-718).
The decreasing-sequence computation writes 'as $\phi_m\leq 0$' while the compared functions are the model functions psi_m (defined at 973) and psi_{2m}; literal symbol usage recorded.
The display contains an extra closing \rangle: \langle -P(...)^{d+1}\rangle_{X/\pdisc}\rangle\na.
The definition of \hat d_1' has an unmatched parenthesis in the E(...) term: E(\hat P(phi0,phi1)_t) is closed once.
The target pairing is written \langle L\an \rangle rather than \langle L_\K^{d+1}\rangle; compare line 1069.

The text describes \cE^1(L) as fiberwise finite-energy log-growth metrics and then speaks of 'the subspace of \cE^1(L) ... relatively maximal'; at line 606 the boundary-data condition is added to the definition of \cE^1(L). Both descriptions coexist.

Boundary data phi_partial is fixed as the restriction to pi^{-1}(S^1) of a smooth psh metric on L, and E^1(L) is then defined with this boundary data, so all results are relative to this fixed choice.
